variantId.description: **What the guest adds to the cart, when there is nothing to choose** (r8, ORDERS-MONEY-C40, the lead's option A): for a product item whose product has one default variant, that variant, resolved from the Pricing price reference the item carries; the add-to-cart asks only the quantity (and a date for a timed product). rewardId.description: For `reward`, a marketing-crm loyalty reward the guest can redeem.

challengeId.description: For `challenge`, a marketing-crm challenge the guest can join.

priceRef.description: The Pricing reference the channel resolves to a price. AI never computes a price.

reasonTemplateKey.description: The template reason (decided 29 September, decision 9): no model writes guest-visible reasons.

confidenceBand.description: Design 5.6: a band, never a bare percentage.

productEvent.description: Product or event the strategy controls

venue.description: Venue's name, through tenancy#scopeRecords by venue_id (ADAM CR-423)

basePriceSource.description: Base price source: the Board 1 price list and rate the strategy moves from, e.g. UAE Standard Admission -> Adult

currentPrice.description: Current resolved dynamic price: the newPrice of the strategy's newest deployed or partiallyDeployed price_execution where the strategy prices one target (singleProduct, or an event with at most one performance); otherwise null (ADAM CR-423)

adjustmentRange.description: Adjustment range allowed by the strategy

automationLevel.description: Automation level, from the most specific dynamic_pricing_control covering the strategy (strategy, product, event, venue, market, global); advisory where there is none (replaces automationMode; ADAM CR-423, CR-417)

status.description: Status: draft, ready (a draft with a ladder and at least one rule, whose scope is not frozen), scheduled (active, with effectiveFrom after now), active, paused, frozen, expired or retired; ready and scheduled are derived, the rest as stored, and testing is not answered (ADAM CR-423; LO-CR423-001)

owner.description: Owner, the owner principal's display name through identity#principalRecords (ADAM CR-423)

parentEventId.description: For grouped events. The parent is an existing event at the same venue, not the event itself, and has no parent of its own (one level; ADAM CR-256). Declared as a key onto `catalogue.event`.

performanceCount.description: How many performances the event has. Counted by the server; never sent by a client.

lifecycleState.description: **Where the event is in its lifecycle** (4 October 2026, CHG-FXC-003; catalogue.event had nowhere to keep it). Written only by `setEventLifecycleState` and the event lifecycle job, which check the transition against `states/event.yaml` (ADAM CR-109); `createEvent` and `cloneEvent` create an event in `draft`. `isActive` stays the switch that hides an event from sale without changing its state.

scheduledLifecycleState.description: **A move waiting for its effectiveFrom** (ADAM CR-109, option 2; CHG-R10CAT-009): written by `setEventLifecycleState` when `effectiveFrom` is in the future, applied and cleared by the event lifecycle job in the workers host at `scheduledLifecycleAt`. Null when nothing waits.

scheduledLifecycleAt.description: When the waiting move is applied (the request's `effectiveFrom`; ADAM CR-109).

scheduledLifecycleReason.description: The reason given with the waiting move, carried on `event.lifecycleChanged` when it is applied (ADAM CR-109).

GuestListing.description: **How a product appears to a guest** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-14). `bookable`: listed and searched while it is on sale, and added to the basket. `infoOnly`: listed and searched with its details, photo and `notBookableLabel` whether or not it is on sale, and **never added to a basket** (`addCartLine` refuses it with `409`); the screen opens its details instead. `hidden`: never listed or searched for a guest, and reachable only where a staff channel sells it. Independent of `isSellable`, which says whether a channel may sell it at all.

productVariantId.description: The variant priced; a variant of productId, required when the product has more than one sellable variant, else 400 validation on productVariantId (ADAM CR-419)

compareChannels.description: Channel Comparison (p.51): run the same transaction through these channels too; empty for none

PriceBreakdownCalculationSimulationExpla.description: **What Price Breakdown, Calculation Simulation & Explainability displays.** Read from the workshop pack's own display and configuration directory for this screen; each property names the sentence it came from. **Not a row** - the screen is a view over the module's existing state.

source.description: Source: the price list, rule, fee or tax profile

rule.description: Rule: id of the rule applied, e.g. FE-021, TAX-UAE-01

components.description: Explainability Panel and Rule Trace (p.51), in sequence

calculationVersion.description: Calculation version used, the calculation profile's code and version (ADAM CR-419)

finalPayable.description: Absent (null) for a channel with no catalogue channel, `api` or `backOffice` (ADAM CR-537): no price list prices the variant there.

difference.description: Why it differs, e.g. Call Center Booking Fee; for `api` or `backOffice`, that no price list prices this variant on that channel (ADAM CR-537)

aiInsights.description: AI observations for this screen; advisory only, never applied automatically. Answered as an empty list until an AI producer exists (ADAM CR-419; LO-CR419-001)

familyKey.description: **The same product at another location** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-18). Optional. A tenant that sells one attraction at several venues gives each venue's product the same key, e.g. `aquarium-entry`; the key names the family across the tenant and each venue has at most one product in it, so a second product at the same venue with the key is refused with `409 duplicate-code`. **What it is for:** when a guest changes location on the booking screen (the 'Booking at' switcher, `BookingFlowConfig.locationSwitcher`), lines whose product shares a `familyKey` with a product at the new venue are carried over to that product, with times and prices refreshed; every other line is cleared. Null means the product belongs to no family and its lines always clear on a switch. Compared case-insensitively, like `code`.

bookingEntry.description: **Which booking screen Book opens** (ADAM CR-591, Chinmay, 3 November 2026; CHG-CR591-001). Worked out on read and never stored; set on every guest or visitor read that answers a product (`listProducts`, `getProduct`) and on every `searchCatalogue` result, null on staff reads, and null when the product has no Book (info-only). In this order: (a) kind `bundle` gives `bundle` while `bundleId` is set; with no such bundle it is null and the card opens Item Detail as now. (b) `requiresTimeWindow` true gives `timeWindow`. (c) Otherwise the product's published booking flow by `getPublishedBookingFlow`'s rule (the product's flow, then its category's, then the venue's enabled default for its kind, with the same tie rule), from `white-label#publishedBookingFlowSteps`: its first enabled step, skipping `location` and `helpMeChoose`; `resourceMap` gives `venueMap`; `date`, `time` or `performance` gives `dateFirst`; any other step gives `productFirst`. If no flow resolves, the same test is applied to the default order of the flow type the kind rule picks. Book opens: `dateFirst` GST-007, `productFirst` GST-008, `venueMap` GST-074, `timeWindow` GST-075, each with `productId`; `bundle` GST-056 with `bundleId`.

bundleId.description: Set only when `bookingEntry` is `bundle` (ADAM CR-591; CHG-CR591-001): the id of the promotions bundle whose `variant_id` is this product's variant, while `getGuestBundle` would return it (published, active, in its window). Never taken from a search result's `id`: for a bundle that is the bundle's catalogue product, not the bundle.

fromPrice.description: **The lowest list price on the caller's channel now** (ADAM CR-358, option (a); CHG-CR358-001): the lowest `listPrice` among the product's sellable variants on the caller's channel, in the same currency as `ProductVariant.listPrice`, by the same price-list rule as `searchCatalogue`'s `fromPrice` and `ProductVariant.listPrice`. Set by `listProducts` (its description says how); not stored and ignored on input. Null where no price list prices it on that channel, and null from every other operation that answers `Product` for now.

displayOrder.description: Where this product sorts among the venue's products in listProducts, lower first. Not alphabetical: the order the venue wants guests to see. (ADAM CR-581, Chinmay, 3 November 2026; CHG-CR581-001.) Stored on `catalogue.product` as `display_order`, nullable with default 100 like `catalogue.product_category.display_order`; existing rows take 100. Set by `createProduct` (100 when not sent) and `updateProduct` (changed only when the body carries it; null stores null), and returned by every operation that answers `Product`, `getProduct` and the till's catalogue bundle included. No back-office product screen shows or edits it.

isFeatured.description: **The plan card's Most popular badge** (ADAM CR-482, decided by Chinmay on 2 November 2026): the venue marks a product featured. Stored on `catalogue.product` as `is_featured`, set by `createProduct` and `updateProduct`, returned by `listProducts` and `getProduct`. WEB-022 shows the badge on a featured plan.

compareAtPrice.description: **What the same visits cost bought singly** (ADAM CR-482): the comparison price behind the plan card's saving. Stored on `catalogue.product` as `compare_at_amount` in the venue's trading currency, set by `createProduct` and `updateProduct`, returned by `listProducts` and `getProduct`. WEB-022 shows the saving as `compareAtPrice` minus `fromPrice` when `compareAtPrice` is the greater; null shows no saving, never a made-up value.

highlightBadge.description: **The card's highlight badge** (ADAM CR-504; Chinmay, 3 November 2026; CHG-CR504-001), e.g. POPULAR or BEST VALUE, keyed by ISO 639-1 code like `LocalisedText`, at most 20 characters per language (longer is `400 validation`). Stored in the nullable jsonb column `catalogue.product.highlight_badge`, set with `createProduct` and `updateProduct` by a caller holding `PRODUCT_CONFIGURE`, and answered by every operation that answers Product, to every audience. WEB-005's card shows the value for the guest's language, falling back to the English value, as the pill on the card image in capitals; null shows no badge.

average.description: The average rating, 1.0 to 5.0, one decimal.

count.description: How many reviews the average is over.

rating.description: **The card's rating summary** (ADAM CR-504; Chinmay, 3 November 2026; CHG-CR504-001): readOnly, not stored on the product. `listProducts` answers it; every other operation answers null. It is null until the rating source is decided, and nothing invents a value meanwhile. WEB-005 shows it as the star line under the display tags (a star, the average, then `count` followed by reviews) whenever it is not null.

nameLocalised.description: **The product's name in each of the tenant's enabled languages** (6 October 2026, CHG-R4-011; the tenant's languages, not the venue's: CHG-R8PRD-009, ADAM CR-213), keyed by ISO 639-1 code, e.g. `{"en": "Aquarium entry", "ar": "دخول الأكواريوم"}`. Every guest surface shows the entry for the guest's language and falls back to `name`, which stays the name staff search and reports print. Null, or a language missing from it, means `name` is shown. At most 200 characters per language, as `name`.

descriptionLocalised.description: The product's description in each language, as `nameLocalised`; falls back to `description` (6 October 2026, CHG-R4-011).

createdByPrincipalId.x-ticvai-staff-only: Omitted from the response when the caller is a guest or a visitor (R164).
createdByPrincipalId.description: 1.4.18. **The approval gate refuses an approver who is the author, and nothing recorded either.** `SeatBlock`, `DelegatedAccess` and `ManualDiscountRequest` all carry this and the product passing through approval did not.

approvedByPrincipalId.x-ticvai-staff-only: Omitted from the response when the caller is a guest or a visitor (R164).

responsibleDepartmentId.description: Who owns this product commercially. A scope node at `department` level.

onSaleFrom.description: 1.4.8. **A seasonal product should not need somebody awake at midnight.** Archiving already runs on a timer in this contract, so the machinery exists; `effectiveFrom` appears on tax codes, FX rates and white-label policies and not here.

onSaleTo.description: Retires the product automatically. **Retirement is not deletion** — the product stops selling and every order that referenced it still resolves.

validTo.description: **The last moment the product's entitlements are valid; null means the same as `onSaleTo`** (ADAM CR-167 as the lead ruled it, 26 October 2026; CHG-R10OPN-003). A season pass stops selling at `onSaleTo` and is used until `validTo`: an entitlement template's `expiryAnchor` of `seasonEnd` ends here (`access#issueOrderEntitlements`). Sales closing is not validity ending.

categoryId.description: **Taken from their `fnb.product` and `retail.product`, 20 September.** `catalogue.product_category` has existed since 20 August with two operations and nothing could be filed under it — a merchandise hierarchy with a tree and no leaves. Their per-domain product tables both carried this column and ours did not.

isSellable.description:
True only when live **and** carried by a published bundle. Approval and publication are different acts.
**Derived, never set.** It changes when `transitionProductLifecycle` moves the product and when `publishBundle` carries it, so `updateProduct` does not take it — `withdraw` is how a product stops selling.

isStockTracked.description: **Taken from their `fnb.product`, 20 September.** Whether a sale decrements stock, which is not what `isSellable` asks. A ticket is sellable and tracks no stock; a bottle of water is both. Without it, an F&B sale cannot tell inventory whether to move.

segmentTags.description:
7.3.5. **A channel and a segment tag are mandatory and nothing required either.** A catalogue that cannot be filtered by segment is a catalogue nobody can report on.
**Hierarchical, not flat** — `family/with-toddlers` narrows `family` without duplicating it, which is how the promotions engine already treats scope.
**A level is a tag under `level/`** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-19): `level/beginner`, `level/intermediate`, `level/advanced`, `level/expert` (proposed codes, client to correct). A guest screen filters on it with `listProducts` `segmentTag`, and the words a guest reads beside each option come from `ProductCategory.description`, not from the tag.

codeSchema.description:
7.3.4 specifies `[ParkCode]-[ProductType]-[Variant]`. **`Product.code` existed and nothing required a format**, so a venue with three thousand products had three thousand conventions.
The tenant sets the pattern and the platform generates against it. **Validation is the point, not the string** — a code typed by hand is a code that will not sort.

entitlementTemplateId.description: What the buyer receives. Null for products that grant nothing — F&B and retail. Identity and entitlement are separate concerns.

blockedOffline.description: True for seated and retail. Seated because a seat map is not a count; retail because stock depletes in real time.

dataMaskValues.description: Custom fields. JSONB-backed, defined by the venue's data mask.

notBookableLabel.description: The label a guest reads on an `infoOnly` product, e.g. *Info only* or *Not bookable online; ask at the desk* (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-14). Each value at most 60 characters. Null means the guest screen shows its default wording. Ignored unless `guestListing` is `infoOnly`.

salesContact.description: **Who a guest contacts to book a view-only product** (decided 29 September, W3), e.g. a training course listed with full details and no Book button. Shown as *Call sales* and *Email sales* on an `infoOnly` product. Null means the venue's own contact (white-label `getTenantAppStatus.contact`). Ignored unless `guestListing` is `infoOnly`.

bookingFlowId.description: **The booking flow this product is sold through** (decided 29 September, W8 and W12): a white-label `BookingFlow` of the venue, which orders the guest's steps (for a workshop, the product first and then the date and time). Null means the category's flow (`ProductCategory.bookingFlowId`), and failing that the venue's flow for the product's `kind`, as white-label `getPublishedBookingFlow`'s kind rule picks it where several of the venue's enabled defaults list the kind (ADAM CR-427, 31 October 2026). A venue that wants a different flow for a product sets this or the category's `bookingFlowId`. Written by `createProduct` and `updateProduct`, which refuse an id that is not a flow of the venue with `422`.

displayTags.description:
**Short facts a guest reads on the ticket card and under *Read more***: *2 Hours*, *Min 1.10 m*, *Free adult entry*, *Valid 90 days*, *Emirates ID* (decided 29 September, 23SEP-3). Not `segmentTags`, which are for reporting and segmentation and which a guest never reads.
**Derived on read when none are set.** When the venue has written no tags, a read returns tags derived from the product's duration (`clock`), entitlement validity (`calendar`) and the eligibility rule's `minHeightCm` (`height`), each marked `derived: true`; they are never stored. Once the venue writes any tag, only what it wrote is returned. Whether the guest screen shows them is `BookingFlowConfig.ticketTags` (white-label).

media.description:
**The product's own photos and video** (decided 29 September, 23SEP-4). *Read more* opens on the `isPrimary` item, and a listing shows each product's primary image, so two tickets in one category no longer share the category's picture (`ProductCategory.imageAssetId`).
Every `assetId` names an asset of the asset library (`assets.yaml` `MediaAsset`) in status `ready` whose kind matches `kind`; anything else is a `422`. **Exactly one item is `isPrimary`** when the list is not empty, and an `assetId` appears once; otherwise `400`. Setting the list records each reference as asset usage (`MediaUsage` with `surface: product`, `referenceId` the product id, `isLive` true while the product is listed to guests), which is what stops a used asset being archived from under the product.

consentQuestionIds.description: **The consent questions a guest answers when booking this product**, in the order they are asked (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-26): *Are you able to swim?*, *Do you hold a scuba certification?*, *I accept the risk*. Each id names a consent question defined in marketing-crm (`ConsentQuestion`), which owns the text, its version and whether it is asked per person or once per booking; the answer is stored there as a consent record (question version, answer, who answered, when). **One question or several, as the venue chooses.** A flow can carry its own list too (`white-label.BookingFlow.settings.consentQuestionIds`, on the product's published booking flow as `getPublishedBookingFlow` resolves it: product, then category, then the venue's flow for the kind; moved from `BookingFlowConfig` 29 September, W12); a booking asks the union of the flow's questions and those of every product in the cart, each question once (`orders.Cart.consentQuestions`). An id that names no active consent question of the tenant is a `422`.

addOnProductIds.description: **The add-ons offered with this product, in display order** (accepted 26 October 2026, Chinmay, ADAM CR-252 option A): each a `kind: addOn` product of the same venue (a coffee break, a working lunch, an AV technician offered with a meeting-room type), set in the back office. `listProducts` answers it, so WEB-048 and GST-075 read a room type's add-ons from the load they already make and fetch those products; the guest adds one as a cart line with `parentLineId`. An id that is not a `kind: addOn` product of the same venue is `400 validation` on `addOnProductIds`. Empty when none is offered.

requiresTimeWindow.description: **True for a space sold by the hour**, e.g. a meeting room type (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-13). The product is the room type (*focus pod*, *majlis*, *boardroom*, *auditorium*), never a named room; its lengths are a `length` axis (`setProductAttributes`) whose values carry `durationMinutes`, and each length is a variant priced on its own in the price list, so price is the room rate for that length. The cart line carries the booked start and end (orders), the end being the start plus the chosen variant's `durationMinutes`; `resources.listProductStartTimes` supplies the start times for a variant and a date and `allocateResources` picks the room from the product's resource requirements (`setExperienceResourceRequirements`) at checkout. True requires every active variant to have a `durationMinutes`; otherwise `422`.

productOwnerPrincipalId.description: The product owner (29 September, data model DM3), set with `setProductContextOwnership`. `responsibleDepartmentId` is the owning department.

operationalContact.description: A principal id or a name, as the context screen takes it.

brandId.description: The brand, as the context screen names it (a catalogue brand category).

eventId.description: **The event this product sells admission to** (4 October 2026, CHG-FXC-011; WEB-002, WEB-004): a product page finds its event and the event's performances (`Performance.eventId`) give it dates. Null for a product not tied to an event (merchandise, a pass, a membership).

createdAt.description: **When the product was created** (ADAM CR-204, option A, decided 25 October 2026; CHG-R10CAT-007): `catalogue.product.created_at`, NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), set by the server and never by a request. Rows that predate it are backfilled by the migration task (the earliest of the product's first version's `published_at` and the migration time), then the NOT NULL and the DEFAULT are set. `listProductLifecycle` orders and filters on it.

updatedAt.description: **When the product last changed** (ADAM CR-204): set by `updateProduct` and by every product sub-resource PUT and bulk change that versions the product; null until the first change after creation. `listProductLifecycle`'s `lastModifiedAt` and `modifiedSince` read it.

ProductDisplayTag.description: One short fact on a ticket card (decided 29 September, 23SEP-3). `kind` picks the icon.

kind.description: `clock` a duration, `height` a height rule, `free` something included free, `calendar` a validity, `id` a document the guest must bring.

label.description: What the guest reads, e.g. *2 Hours*. Each language value at most 40 characters.

derived.description: True on a tag the server derived on read because the venue set none. Never sent.

ProductKind.description:
**`openDated` added 24 August** from the client's *Create Ticket Flow* board, which names six main ticket types and this was the one with no kind: **valid on any date within an eligible range, rather than for a named performance or a fixed date.**
The mechanism already existed — `access.entitlement` carries `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `entries_allowed` and `frozen_days`, which is exactly an open-dated pass. **What was missing was the product saying it is one**, so a catalogue could not offer it and a report could not count it.
**`datedAdmission` is a different thing and the two were being conflated**: dated is *this Tuesday*, open-dated is *any Tuesday between March and June*. A guest buying the second and being sold the first has bought the wrong ticket.
**Transport uses two existing kinds, not a new one** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-21). A one-way trip is `timedAdmission`: `transport.createTransportRoute` creates the route's product with one variant per passenger type, and each departure is a performance. A multi-trip or unlimited pass is `openDated`: `transport.createTransportPassType` creates it, with `EntitlementTemplate.entriesAllowed` = the pass's trips (null for unlimited), the validity = `validityDays`, and `EntitlementTemplate.transportRestriction` naming the station pair the pass was bought for, so `access` refuses it on another journey. The sale path is unchanged: both are cart lines, priced by `transport.quoteTransportFare` (orders `TransportLineAttributes`).

**`walletTopUp` added 20 October 2026** (r8 re-walk, CHG-R8RW-001): the product a wallet top-up is sold as, so the money for a top-up is taken on an order like any other sale and `createPayment` has its `orderId`. A venue has one, with one variant. Orders prices its line at the line's `quotedUnitPrice` (the amount being loaded; no tax, since stored value is a liability and not a supply), and the line may share a sale with anything else (the client-approved till's "Add top-up to sale", CHG-R8RW-009); once the order is paid, wallet `topUpWallet` credits that line's amount, once per line. A value added to a response enum, so a breaking change under ADR-0026, approved as BC-460 to BC-462; a client that does not know it shows the product as a plain product.

ProductMedia.description: One photo or video of a product, referencing the asset library (decided 29 September, 23SEP-4). One row per product and asset, so the asset library can answer which products use an asset.

isPrimary.description: The item *Read more* opens on and a listing shows. Exactly one per product.

url.description: **The asset's stable CDN address, for a guest card** (ADAM CR-221, option A, decided 25 October 2026; CHG-R10CAT-014): the asset library's public address for the asset, set on guest-facing reads (`searchCatalogue`, `listProducts` and `getProduct` for a guest or a visitor) when the asset is public and `ready`, as `getPublishedTenantConfig` returns white-label assets (`brandUrls`). Null otherwise, and on staff reads, which are unchanged. Catalogue reads the asset in process, a read the lead granted across deployables (XDR-005, 25 October 2026; CHG-R10CAT-015).

thumbnailUrl.description: The asset library's thumbnail address for the asset, on the same reads and with the same rule as `url` (ADAM CR-221).

ProductSalesContact.description: Who to contact to book a view-only product (decided 29 September, W3). At least one of `phone` or `email`.

note.description: A line shown under the contact, e.g. *Group courses are booked by phone*. At most 200 characters per language.

listPrice.description: **The list price on the caller's channel now**, resolved on read from the price lists (`listProductVariants`; R8 blocker cause GPS-C27, CHG-R8SPN-028). Not stored on the variant and ignored on input. Null where no price list prices it on that channel. The list price, not the total: promotions and bundles are applied at the basket.

referencePrice.description: **The price a saving is measured against** (accepted 26 October 2026, Chinmay, ADAM CR-253 option C), set by the back office on the variant (`updateProductVariant`). Null where the variant claims no saving, which is the default. In the same currency as `listPrice`.

savingPercent.description: **Computed by the server, never in the browser** (ADAM CR-253): with a `referencePrice` and a `listPrice` below it, the whole percent the list price saves, `floor((referencePrice - listPrice) / referencePrice * 100)` (rounded down, so the label never overstates; proposed, client to correct); null otherwise. A length tile shows *Save n%* only when this is set.

name.description: **Taken from their variant tables, 20 September.** `axisValues` gives `{size: L}` and no string a guest can read. A menu showing *Large* needs somewhere for the word to live.

barcode.description: **Taken from their variant tables, 20 September.** `catalogue.alternative_code` is a partner's own code for a variant and **requires `partnerId`**, so a manufacturer's EAN had nowhere to go. One per variant against many per variant is a different cardinality and belongs in a different place — and a POS scan should be an indexed column lookup, not a join.

isDefault.description: Taken from their variant tables. Which variant a product page opens on. Ours had no way to say, so a three-size drink opened on whichever row sorted first.

isActive.description: False when retired. Retired variants are never deleted — orders reference them.

priceCategoryId.description: The variant's price category, a `catalogue.price_category` id (ADAM CR-455): the winning price assignment's category rate for it replaces the price (`catalogue#variantPriceRecords`); null for none. Set by `updateProductVariant`.

description.description: **Who this ticket type is for and what it includes**, shown behind the (i) on each Adult, Child, Senior or Infant row (decided 29 September, 23SEP-6). Each language value at most 300 characters; longer is a `400`. Set with `updateProductVariant`. Whether the guest screen shows it is `BookingFlowConfig.cardInfo` (white-label).

RevenueOptimizationCommandCenterSummary.x-ticvai-persistence: none — projection; the headline tiles over the list, computed at read time for the filters in force
RevenueOptimizationCommandCenterSummary.description: **The headline figures on Revenue Optimization Command Center.** The pack's KPI cards, split out of the row (decided 29 September, readiness close-out): a count describes the list, not each item in it.

approvalRequired.description: Approval Required: changes waiting for an approver

forecastAccuracy.description: Forecast Accuracy over the last 30 days (decided 29 September, readiness close-out), percent

optimizationSuccessRate.description: Optimization Success Rate: executed changes with a positive measured outcome, percent

aiRevenueBrief.description: AI Revenue Brief, e.g. AED 284,000 of opportunity in the next seven days. Advisory only: generated narrative never changes a price (decided 29 September, readiness close-out)

RevenueOptimizationCommandCenterView.x-ticvai-persistence: none — projection over catalogue state, assembled at read time from tables that already exist
RevenueOptimizationCommandCenterView.description: **What Revenue Optimization Command Center displays.** Read from the workshop pack's own display and configuration directory for this screen; each property names the sentence it came from. **Not a row** - the screen is a view over the module's existing state.

automationMode.description: Automation Mode in force for this scope

approvalStatus.description: Approval Status: notRequired, pending, approved or rejected. notRequired where the latest execution's source is conditionalAutonomous or autonomous; else pending for pending, sentToSimulation or sentForApproval, approved for accepted or modified, rejected for rejected (ADAM CR-408)

executionStatus.description: Execution Status: notStarted, queued, processing, live, partial, failed or rolledBack, from the latest price_execution: scheduled queued, executing processing, deployed live, partiallyDeployed partial, failed failed, reverted rolledBack, none notStarted (ADAM CR-408)

revenueRisk.description: Revenue Risk if no action is taken

eventProximity.description: Event Proximity: days until the event

nextAction.description: Suggested next action (the pack's Action column)

rank.description: Ordering for best-seat assignment. Lower is better.

priceBands.description: What a seat in this category costs, by band (decided 28 September, audit R275 (d), from the BO-1045 pack). Written by `createSeatCategory` and `updateSeatCategory`. A band may be narrowed to a sales channel or a customer segment and to a window; where several match a sale, the narrowest wins.

SeatPriceBand.description: One price band on a seat category (decided 28 September, audit R275 (d)). The currency is `amount.currency`, resolved from the region like every `Money` (ADR-0018), so the band carries no currency of its own.

scopePath.description: Where the row is owned: the path of the scope that wrote it (its venue, or the region or tenant that configured it), set by the server from the caller's scope and never taken from a request. Row-level security reads it, so a venue writes and reads its own rows (MOD audit, 14 October 2026, CHG-MOD-007).

customerSegmentId.description: A `marketing-crm` customer segment; null means everyone.
